title: Explore: Governance and release gates
description: Inspect current-head release governance, summary artifacts, and blocking semantics around version consistency, evidence freshness, and release scorecards.
findings: Current-head release authority is coherent on paper but `release-check-summary.md` is `NO_GO` with blocking failures in version consistency, desktop checks, stale acceptance evidence, and unresolved triage semantics. `delivery_gate.py` and `check_authority_alignment.py` pass, so the blocker cluster is closure, not missing governance surfaces.

title: Explore: Desktop capability and sidecar contract
description: Inspect the current desktop runtime/packaging contract, Tauri capability boundary, sidecar validator expectations, and actual strict validation result on this head.
findings: Desktop contract currently fails in two different ways: `validate_sidecar_contract.cjs` requires frontend permissions to be exactly `core:default`, but `desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/main-desktop.json` also grants updater/fs permissions; separately `build:sidecar` fails while hydrating `desktop/src-tauri/bin/sidecar/node_modules` due to native dependency install errors under the bundled Node 20 target.

title: Explore: Workflow triage blocker semantics
description: Inspect how unresolved triage is computed and whether the blocker semantics are aligned with the current repository state.
findings: `scripts/release_check_summary.py` treats any linked triage state not in `{resolved,rejected}` as blocking, but the current scan reports `state_files_scanned=385`, `linked_triage_records=115`, `unresolved_triage_records=115`, and `invalid_state_files=270`, while a direct scan of `.workflow/active/*/.data/state.json` in this checkout found no current unresolved triage record that could be reproduced from parseable state files.

title: Score: Feasibility
description: Score feasibility for closing the current-head blockers with evidence from exploration findings.
findings: The blocker set is technically feasible to close because the failures are localized to version authority alignment, desktop contract policy/code mismatch, sidecar packaging pipeline stability, stale retained evidence refresh, and triage blocker computation. No evidence suggests a missing architectural primitive.
recommendations: Make one authority decision for release version ownership, then align desktop metadata or adjust the checker. Reconcile `validate_sidecar_contract.cjs` with `main-desktop.json` by either narrowing permissions to core-only or updating the documented/validated boundary. Refresh retained release evidence only after gate fixes land. Audit `unresolved_triage_blocker_signal` against parseable active states and decide whether invalid files should block separately from unresolved states.

title: Score: Impact
description: Score impact of closing the blockers on release readiness and customer delivery confidence.
findings: Closing this set directly affects the repo's ability to claim `GO` on the current head. It removes false/noisy blockers, restores desktop release proof, and aligns machine-readable evidence with the actual shipped contract.
recommendations: Prioritize blockers that feed multiple failing checks: version authority and desktop sidecar/package validation unlock several scorecard dimensions at once. Treat retained evidence refresh as the final step, not the first.

title: Score: Risk
description: Score risk with evidence: failure modes, regression potential, and release ambiguity.
findings: Risk is elevated because the current release artifact says `NO_GO`, the desktop boundary validator and capability file disagree, and stale acceptance artifacts are being interpreted as current proof. There is also risk of changing release semantics incorrectly if triage blocker logic is loosened without a precise target state definition.
recommendations: Do not refresh evidence before fixing the underlying failures, or the repo will retain same-head but still red proof. Any change to triage semantics must preserve the invariant that real unresolved execution states remain blocking.

title: Score: Complexity
description: Score integration complexity across release scripts, desktop packaging, and docs.
findings: Complexity is moderate-to-high because the failures span Python governance scripts, TypeScript package versions, Tauri capability config, sidecar packaging, and release docs. However, the integration points are explicit and already covered by named scripts/tests.
recommendations: Sequence the closure as: version authority -> desktop capability/validator contract -> sidecar/package gate rerun -> retained evidence refresh -> triage semantics reconciliation -> docs final alignment.

title: Score: Alignment
description: Score alignment with project vision, roadmap, and existing authority docs.
findings: The requested closure work is strongly aligned with the current release contract because the existing docs already declare sidecar readiness, same-head evidence freshness, and authority alignment as blocking P0 signals.
recommendations: Keep README / `docs/release/RELEASE_NOTES.md` / `docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md` aligned to one current-head contract. Avoid introducing a second notion of 'good enough' local proof.

title: Score: Maintainability
description: Score maintainability with evidence: clarity, testability, and refactoring safety.
findings: Maintainability is mixed: the repo has explicit scripts and artifacts for each gate, which is good, but current authority is split across `src-ts` and `desktop` version surfaces, and the desktop capability validator now encodes a boundary narrower than the checked-in capability file.
recommendations: After closure, keep one explicit authority per concept: one release version source, one desktop capability boundary contract, one retained-evidence refresh path, and one triage-blocker definition with regression tests.

title: Decision Synthesis
description: Compile scores into analysis.md/context.md/conclusions.json and formulate go/no-go plus closure ordering.
findings: Current-head verdict remains `NO_GO`. The most credible blocker chain is: version authority mismatch (`src-ts` 9.2.5 vs desktop 9.13.0), desktop capability validator mismatch, Node sidecar packaging failure during dependency hydration, stale retained release evidence bound to older head/version, and triage blocker accounting that currently reports unresolved records without a reproducible active-state anchor in this checkout.
recommendations: Lock the closure order and do not regenerate retained acceptance evidence until version + desktop gate failures are fixed. Then rerun release summary so `release-readiness-artifact.json` becomes fresh same-head proof instead of superseded evidence.
